newsitem.title: UK: C&W sees no imminent global alliance deal.
newsitem.headline: C&W sees no imminent global alliance deal.

text.p: Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc (CW) said on Friday it saw no imminent link-up with a global alliance after abandoning its telecoms partnership with German utilities VEBA AG and RWE.

Asked whether C&W would consider joining Global One, the alliance of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint, or any other grouping, a spokeswoman said: "We shall only do so if, after careful consideration, we are certain that it will add shareholder value. In any event, don't expect anything to happen quickly."
Analysts have tipped Global One as the most obvious partner for Cable and Wireless, which has valuable access to Asian and British telecoms markets.

In the meantime, C&W denied that it was pulling out of Europe after abandoning its German telecoms partnership, its second largest investment in Europe, because VEBA was committed to large-scale investments in Germany and elsewhere in Europe.
C&W also believed it had too little management control over the German venture, called Vebacom.
"Europe is still attractive to Cable and Wireless and it is a very important market," the company spokeswoman said.

Under divorce terms with VEBA, the German company paid 2.21 billion marks to C&W to buy back its 45 percent stake in Vebacom -- 29 million marks more than C&W paid for it two years ago. C&W is also buying back VEBA's 50 percent stake in its loss-making Cable and Wireless Europe SA unit for 90 million marks.
C&W said it was not giving up on the German market but that it preferred to concentrate on its UK-based Cable and Wireless Communications venture with three other cable companies.
Its Cable and Wireless Europe unit is incorporated in Belgium and has operations in eight European countries -- Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain and Switzerland.

The business, which will now be wholly owned by C&W, had revenues of 26 million pounds and accrued lossses before tax of 16 million pounds in the six months to September 30 1996. Net assets were 27 million pounds.
The business provides telecoms services such as customised networks and leased lines. It also supplies and maintains customer equipment and messaging services.
